citations.description: Ticket comment by RebarBotNava: 'I did NOT run a local full-suite count, so I am not attesting a count. The evidence is CI: the full suite passed on four clean checkouts (ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 + macos py3.13) yielding Verified +1 on the merged patchset.'

findings.criterion: [operator-attested] the full suite passes with a test count equal to the pre-split count, evidenced by the two pytest summary lines quoted in a comment
findings.detail: The criterion requires the two pytest summary lines to be quoted in a ticket comment. The only comment on the ticket explicitly states: 'I did NOT run a local full-suite count, so I am not attesting a count.' No pytest summary lines are quoted anywhere in the ticket. The CI reference (Gerrit change 1426, Verified +1) is a specific reference but does not satisfy the criterion's explicit evidence form — the criterion demands the pytest summary lines themselves, not a CI vote.
findings.remediation: Record the two pytest summary lines (e.g. 'N passed, N warnings in Xs') from a full suite run as a ticket comment, naming the run date and environment. The Gerrit Verified +1 on change 1426 (dc26a34e399) is supporting context but does not substitute for the quoted pytest output the criterion requires.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
